From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p99 jump + elevated errors on Hosted API (Skyline account)

Triage notes (preliminary):
- I pulled the host-side telemetry for Skyline's route on the us-west fleet. Seeing repeated GPU memory allocation failures (cudaMalloc returning out-of-memory) on a small subset of nodes starting 08:48 PT. When that happens the runtime falls back to a CPU path or restarts the worker process — both introduce large tail latency spikes.
- Memory profiles show a gradual fragmentation pattern on affected kernels; peak resident set stays under physical RAM but allocation attempts for KV-cache / attention buffers are failing.
- Correlation: notable increase in long-context requests (seq length > 2048) from Skyline's traffic in same window; KV cache growth exacerbates fragmentation.

Attached: trimmed heap dump and an excerpt of the allocation trace (gpu_heap_dump_20260601.log). Relevant log excerpt: 

    2026-06-01T08:48:12Z [worker-12] WARN cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (attempt 3)
    2026-06-01T08:48:13Z [worker-12] ERROR runtime: falling back to cpu backend for request id=5f3a2
    2026-06-01T08:48:13Z [worker-12] WARN perf: request latency=3120ms (cpu fallback)

Immediate next steps I'm pushing now:
1) Isolate affected nodes and cordon them from routing.
2) Force eviction of long-idle KV caches on worker restart.
3) Roll model route to a slightly older variant with conservative kv-sizing for the next 30 minutes while we stabilize.

I'll post updates as I have them. Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: gpu_heap_dump_20260601.log]
